source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #357 (branch fix/320-resource-validation at head 0c4ce204c042fb8edcb33c36f140e127d2aad6bd — the #320 change with its two Codex P2 fixes (a sub-ascribed type export registers its fresh face identity in the type index and export info, and the export (sub resource) ascription check accepts abstract resource faces), merged with current main 98e93a3 (PR #349); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45618907911, 45618925036 and 45618939244 against the branch and pull-request run 45618917159, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #357 after merging PR #349 (main at 98e93a3). The baseline files conflicted in the merge and were resolved by taking main’s baseline as this campaign’s base. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45618952163, 45618969889 and 45618983894 on main at 98e93a3; all three runs pass the gate against main’s checked-in baseline, and the main control is byte-identical to that baseline on all 32 gated series). This PR’s own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +3,432 B (component), +3,432 B (wasi) and +3,416 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +3,040 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +2,224 B / +2,224 B / +2,208 B and stripped .text +1,840 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline, so those twelve are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.56% (2,433,656 B to 2,715,080 B); the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
